title: Coefficient comparison for compactly supported direct image
statement:
Let $f\colon X\to Y$ be a morphism of standing schemes, $f=p\circ j$ a
compactification ($j$ an open immersion, $p$ proper), so that $Rf_!=Rp_*j_!$
([sk-thm-existence] (2)), and let $\Lambda\to\Lambda'$ be a listed coefficient map. For
$K\in\Dctf(X,\Lambda)$ the composite
$$
\gamma^!_{f,K}\colon(Rf_!K)_{\Lambda'}=(Rp_*j_!K)_{\Lambda'}\xrightarrow{\gamma_{p,j_!K}}Rp_*\bigl((j_!K)_{\Lambda'}\bigr)\simeq Rp_*j_!(K_{\Lambda'})=Rf_!(K_{\Lambda'})
$$
is an isomorphism in $\Dctf(Y,\Lambda')$. It does not depend on the
compactification and is compatible with the composition isomorphisms
$R(gf)_!\simeq Rg_!Rf_!$.

proof.text: Write $T^V=(-)_{\Lambda'}$ and write $\delta_{a,M}:T(a_!M)\xrightarrow{\sim}a_!T(M)$ for [det-prop-scalar-six-pullback] (2). All schemes appearing in a compactification are standing schemes, hence qcqs ([sk-def-sfb-dc-setting]); its open immersion is quasi-compact by the definition of compactification [sk-def-nagata-sketch-data]. Apply [det-sf-comp-coherence-single] to the compactification $X\xrightarrow{j}\overline X\xrightarrow{\mathrm{id}}\overline X$ of $j$: it gives $j_!K\in\Dctf(\overline X,\Lambda)$, including finite Tor amplitude. Thus [det-prop-scalar-six-direct-image] (1) for $p$ makes $\gamma_{p,j_!K}$ an isomorphism. Composing with $Rp_*\delta_{j,K}$ gives the displayed $\gamma^!_{f,K}$. By [sk-thm-existence] (2), $Rf_!K\in\Dctf(Y,\Lambda)$; [det-prop-scalar-six-ctf] (3) gives both $T^Y Rf_!K\in\Dctf(Y,\Lambda')$ and $T^XK\in\Dctf(X,\Lambda')$. Applying existence again to $T^XK$ puts $Rf_!T^XK$ in the same target category.

source.place: Isomorphism; use the compactification-model lemma also for finite Tor amplitude

proof.text: We use the normalization of the open comparisons explicitly. Put $T^V=(-)_{\Lambda'}$ and $\delta_{a,M}:T(a_!M)\xrightarrow{\sim}a_!T(M)$. For an open $a$, [def-sfb-derived-open-immersion-shriek-iso] defines this as the conjugate of the restriction-of-scalars/pullback comparison. Expanding the conjugate and restricting by $a^*$, its unit and counit cancel by the triangle identities. Under the open-unit identifications $a^*a_!\simeq\mathrm{id}$, its restriction is therefore the coefficient comparison for the identity pullback, hence the identity under [det-prop-scalar-six-pullback] (1). Also $\gamma_{\mathrm{id},M}=\mathrm{id}$: in its unit/pullback/counit definition [det-prop-scalar-six-direct-image], the identity-pullback comparison and the adjunction triangle identities cancel all three factors.

source.place: Independence: normalization of the two comparisons on the open

proof.text:
Consider dense compactifications $c=(j:X\to Z,p:Z\to Y)$ and $c'=(j':X\to Z',p':Z'\to Y)$ and a proper refinement $h:Z'\to Z$ with $p'=ph$ and $h^{-1}(X)=X$. Let $e_{h,K}:j_!K\to Rh_*j'_!K$ be [det-sf-comp-coherence-refinement]. We prove
$$Rh_*\delta_{j',K}\circ\gamma_{h,j'_!K}\circ T_Z(e_{h,K})=e_{h,T_XK}\circ\delta_{j,K}.$$
The source is $T_Zj_!K\simeq j_!T_XK$, and the target restricts to $T_XK$. By the adjunction and uniqueness in [det-sf-comp-coherence-refinement] (1), it suffices to restrict to $X$. Apply [lem-sfb-proper-direct-image-coefficient-restriction] to $h$ and the open $X\subset Z$, with $M=j'_!K$, which is in $\Dctf$ by step 1 applied to $j'$. It identifies the restricted $\gamma_h$ with $\gamma_{\mathrm{id},K}=\mathrm{id}$. The restrictions of both $e$ maps are identities by the refinement lemma, and those of the $\delta$ maps are identities by step 2. Both sides restrict to $\mathrm{id}_{T_XK}$, proving the equation. Put $\phi_{h,K}=Rp_*e_{h,K}$. Naturality and the proper-composition equation in [det-prop-scalar-six-direct-image] (2), followed by the equation just proved, give
$$\phi_{h,T_XK}\circ\gamma^{!,c}_{f,K}=\gamma^{!,c'}_{f,K}\circ T_Y(\phi_{h,K}).$$

source.place: Independence: the coefficient/refinement identity and its proper pushforward

proof.text: An arbitrary compactification can first be replaced by its schematic closure of $X$. Its ambient scheme is Noetherian by [lem-weil-pbc-finite-type-over-noetherian], since it is finite type over the field $k$. For the closed inclusion $i:Z_0\to Z$ and induced dense open $j_0:X\to Z_0$, [sk-lem-nagata-density-normalization] identifies $j_!K\simeq Ri_*j_{0!}K$ and their proper pushforwards. Use the canonical identification normalized by its restriction to $X$; it is the map $e_i$ adjoint to the open identity under $j_!\dashv j^*$ of [def-sfb-derived-open-immersion-shriek-iso]. The restriction of its target is $K$ by the density-normalization identification. The calculation of step 3 uses density only to have the stated refinement map and its open identification; for this closed $i$, those are instead supplied by density normalization and this adjunction. Its coefficient equation follows by exactly the same restriction calculation: apply [lem-sfb-proper-direct-image-coefficient-restriction] to $i$ over $X$, where its base change is the identity, and use step 2 for $\delta_j,\delta_{j_0}$. Applying $Rp_*$ and the naturality/composition equation of [det-prop-scalar-six-direct-image] (2) gives the coefficient square for the normalization isomorphism as well.

source.place: Independence: reduction of nondense compactifications to their schematic closures

proof.text: For two dense compactifications choose a common refinement by [prop-compactification-refinement], and normalize that refinement by step 4. All these schemes and maps satisfy the standing finite-type and separated hypotheses. For either proper map $h:Z_3\to Z_a$, [lem-weil-pbc-proper-open-section] says the copy of $X$ is open and closed in $h^{-1}(X)$. Density in $Z_3$ implies density in this open inverse image; closedness then implies $h^{-1}(X)=X$ as open subschemes. Thus step 3 applies to both refinement maps. They are isomorphisms and transitive by [det-sf-comp-coherence-refinement] (2),(3). The common-refinement comparisons are independent of the choice and satisfy the cocycle identity by [det-sf-comp-coherence-cocycle]. The two commuting coefficient squares of step 3 therefore give the commuting square for the canonical comparison between the two dense models. Step 4 supplies the squares for normalizing either original model. Pasting these squares proves independence for all compactifications.

source.place: Independence: common dense refinements and passage to arbitrary models

proof.text:
Choose compactifications $f=pj$ and $g=qi$, with $j:X\to\overline X$ and $i:Y\to\overline Y$ open. Compactify $ip$ densely as $\overline X\xrightarrow{j'}W\xrightarrow{r}\overline Y$ and put $A=j_!K$. By [det-sf-comp-composition-interchange], $r^{-1}(Y)=\overline X$, $r|_{\overline X}=p$, and there is a unique map $\iota_A:i_!Rp_*A\to Rr_*j'_!A$ restricting to $\mathrm{id}_{Rp_*A}$; it is an isomorphism for $A\in\Dctf$. We claim
$$Rr_*\delta_{j',A}\circ\gamma_{r,j'_!A}\circ T_{\overline Y}(\iota_A)=\iota_{T_{\overline X}A}\circ i_!\gamma_{p,A}\circ\delta_{i,Rp_*A}.$$
Restrict to $Y$. By [lem-sfb-proper-direct-image-coefficient-restriction] for $r$ and $Y\subset\overline Y$, the restricted proper comparison is $\gamma_{p,A}$. The $\iota$ restrictions are identities by the interchange statement; the $\delta$ restrictions are identities by step 2. Both sides consequently restrict to $\gamma_{p,A}$. This is an isomorphism by [det-prop-scalar-six-direct-image] (1), since $A\in\Dctf$ by step 1. Identify the source with $i_!Rp_*T_{\overline X}A$ using $i_!\gamma_{p,A}\circ\delta_i$. Both maps now restrict to the identity of $Rp_*T_{\overline X}A$, so uniqueness in the interchange statement (2) proves the equation.

source.place: Composition: coefficient compatibility of proper/open interchange

proof.text:
On these models the canonical compact-support compositor is
$$\alpha_{g,f}:Rq_*i_!Rp_*j_!\xrightarrow{Rq_*\iota}Rq_*Rr_*j'_!j_!\simeq R(qr)_*(j'j)_!.$$
Its first arrow is the isomorphism of [det-sf-comp-composition-interchange] (3); the last arrow composes proper direct images and open extensions. Apply $Rq_*$ to the equation of step 6. The naturality square of $\gamma_q$ moves $T(Rq_*\iota)$ across $\gamma_q$. The composition equation of [det-prop-scalar-six-direct-image] (2) then replaces $Rq_*\gamma_r\circ\gamma_q$ by $\gamma_{qr}$. The open-composition equation of [det-prop-scalar-six-pullback] (2) replaces $j'_!\delta_j\circ\delta_{j',j_!K}$ by $\delta_{j'j}$. Thus the two paths from $T Rq_*i_!Rp_*j_!K$ to $R(qr)_*(j'j)_!TK$ agree, giving
$$\gamma^!_{gf,K}\circ T(\alpha_{g,f,K})=\alpha_{g,f,TK}\circ Rg_!(\gamma^!_{f,K})\circ\gamma^!_{g,Rf_!K}.$$
Step 5 identifies the comparison for the model $(j'j,qr)$ with that for any chosen model of $gf$. The compositor here is precisely the model construction from proper/open interchange, with its canonical proper/open composition identifications. All coefficient-comparison inputs lie in $\Dctf$ by step 1 and [sk-thm-existence] (2), so the displayed equation proves the asserted composition compatibility on the required category.

split_report.summary: Continued the interrupted sandbox, retaining its proof and historical searches. Extracted the non-elementary coefficient/open-restriction compatibility as one self-contained statement-only node, removed its nonexistent proper-base-change dependency, and used it explicitly in the refinement, schematic-closure and interchange arguments. Expanded the open-unit normalization and recorded the typed coefficient equations and final pasting. The item statement and existing blueprint and audit metadata are unchanged.
split_report.blueprint: Steps 1, 2–5 and 6–7 realize respectively the Isomorphism, Independence and Composition paragraphs of the current blueprint proof. The new node exposes the open-restriction compatibility implicit in the Independence and Composition paragraphs; no unit route is replaced.

reviewed.note: mechanical checks by tools/merge_delivery.py; mathematics reviewed in full by NT-cc-Q122-8ab86e5c3 (reviewer sub-agent of L); spot-checked: I read all of it in full: the item, the blueprint statement and proof (main-20261015, sk-prop-scalar-six/det-prop-scalar-six-compact-support.md and .proof.md), unit step 4, the new node, and every cited node's statement. The item statement is unchanged and verbatim the blueprint's. Steps 1-7 follow the blueprint's Isomorphism, Independence and Composition paragraphs. Step 1: coherence-single applied to j with the identity proper factor gives j_!K in Dctf; this replaces sk-thm-sf-ctf-stability, which is not a DAG node. Step 2: the mate/triangle-identity normalization of delta and of gamma_id is genuinely elementary. Steps 3-4: the new node is applied with base change equal to the identity, uniqueness comes from refinement (1) over Lambda', and the schematic-closure case goes through density-normalization plus Noetherianity. Step 5: h^{-1}(X)=X follows from the clopen-section lemma plus density, which is exactly the refinement lemma's hypothesis; cocycle gives independence of the choice. Steps 6-7: interchange (1) gives r^{-1}(Y)=Xbar and r restricted equals p, so the new node turns the restriction of gamma_r into gamma_p; uniqueness (2) and pasting with direct-image (2) and pullback (2) composition finish. The typing of every displayed equation checks. The new node lem-sfb-proper-direct-image-coefficient-restriction is true: open restriction commutes with Rp_* by localization, and both sides of the equation are mates of the same pullback square. It is statement-only and self-contained, and passes the edge cases empty V, V=Y, p=id, M=0 and a non-flat finite-ring map. It is not a restated clause (D1) and not a duplicate: closest are lem-weil-pbc-ringed-projection-restriction (the projection map, not gamma) and lem-sf-proper-open-coefficient-refinement (an etale finite-ring D^+ refinement equation). No blueprint node states it, and the Mathlib searches cover all three kinds. I accept the eight tool uses, the same as on the base node. Two minor elementary imprecisions need no fix: step 2 names delta via pullback (2), which is identified with the definition node only in that node's proof and in unit step 2; and step 4 takes the density-normalization identification to be e_i. No SGA is cited.
